title: Maximum Alternating Sum of Squares
summary: Given an integer array nums, you can rearrange its elements in any order.
statement: Given an integer array nums, you can rearrange its elements in any order. The alternating score is calculated as follows: score = nums[0]^2 - nums[1]^2 + nums[2]^2 - nums[3]^2 + ·s Determine the maximum possible alternating score by choosing the best arrangement of the elements in nums.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 signed integers.
Rearrange every value, then add squares at even positions and subtract squares at odd positions.
hints: Only squared magnitudes matter, and the number of positive and negative slots is fixed.
Assign the largest squares to positive even positions and the smallest squares to negative odd positions.
Sort all squares, subtract the first floor(n/2), and add the remainder.
Any arrangement with a smaller square in a positive slot and a larger one in a negative slot improves by swapping them.
editorial: Any arrangement with a smaller square in a positive slot and a larger one in a negative slot improves by swapping them.

tests.explanation: Place squares four and nine in positive positions and square one in a negative position, giving twelve.
Assign the three largest squares to positive positions for score sixteen.
